narrator.name: Narrator
narrator.note: The evangelist Matthew; orderly, weighty storytelling, grave through the Passion.

jesus.name: Jesus
jesus.note: The Lord; prophetic and solemn in the parables of judgment, sorrowful yet resolute in the Passion, majestic after the Resurrection.

chief-priests.name: The chief priests and ancients
chief-priests.note: Temple leaders with the ancients (and, at the tomb request, the Pharisees); scheming, contemptuous of Judas, mocking at the cross.

judas.name: Judas Iscariot
judas.note: The betrayer; bargaining and furtive, falsely warm in his greeting, then despairing.

bystanders.name: Bystanders
bystanders.note: Those standing by: pressing Peter in the courtyard; mishearing Jesus' cry at the cross.

pilate.name: Pontius Pilate
pilate.note: The Roman governor; cool, puzzled, yielding to the crowd, curt with the priests.

pilates-wife.name: Pilate's wife
pilates-wife.note: The governor's wife, sending an urgent warning after a troubling dream.

crowd.name: The crowd
crowd.note: The people before Pilate, stirred up by the chief priests; shouting.

soldiers.name: The soldiers
soldiers.note: Roman soldiers of the governor's band; coarse mock homage.

passers-by.name: Passers-by at the cross
passers-by.note: People passing Golgotha, wagging their heads and taunting.

centurion.name: The centurion
centurion.note: Roman officer at the cross, with his men; awed, frightened confession.

1.t: And when morning was come, all the chief priests and ancients of the people took counsel against Jesus, that they might put him to death.

2.t: And they brought him bound and delivered him to Pontius Pilate the governor.

3.t: Then Judas, who betrayed him, seeing that he was condemned, repenting himself, brought back the thirty pieces of silver to the chief priests and ancients,

4.t: I have sinned in betraying innocent blood.
What is that to us? Look thou to it.

5.t: And casting down the pieces of silver in the temple, he departed and went and hanged himself with an halter.

6.t: But the chief priests having taken the pieces of silver, said:
It is not lawful to put them into the corbona, because it is the price of blood.

7.t: And after they had consulted together, they bought with them the potter's field, to be a burying place for strangers.

8.t: For this cause that field was called Haceldama, that is, the field of blood, even to this day.

9.t: Then was fulfilled that which was spoken by Jeremias the prophet, saying: And they took the thirty pieces of silver, the price of him that was prized, whom they prized of the children of Israel.

10.t: And they gave them unto the potter's field, as the Lord appointed to me.

11.t: And Jesus stood before the governor, and the governor asked him, saying:
Art thou the king of the Jews?

12.t: And when he was accused by the chief priests and ancients, he answered nothing.

13.t: Dost not thou hear how great testimonies they allege against thee?

14.t: And he answered him to never a word, so that the governor wondered exceedingly.

15.t: Now upon the solemn day the governor was accustomed to release to the people one prisoner, whom they would.

16.t: And he had then a notorious prisoner that was called Barabbas.

17.t: They therefore being gathered together, Pilate said:
Whom will you that I release to You: Barabbas, or Jesus that is called Christ?

18.t: For he knew that for envy they had delivered him.

19.t: And as he was sitting in the place of judgment, his wife sent to him, saying:
Have thou nothing to do with that just man; for I have suffered many things this day in a dream because of him.
19.q: a message sent through a messenger; given to its author, like a letter read out

20.t: But the chief priests and ancients persuaded the people that they should ask Barabbas and make Jesus away.

21.t: And the governor answering, said to them:
Whether will you of the two to be released unto you?

22.t: What shall I do then with Jesus that is called Christ?

23.t: Why, what evil hath he done?
But they cried out the more, saying:

24.t: And Pilate seeing that he prevailed nothing, but that rather a tumult was made, taking water washed his hands before the people, saying:
I am innocent of the blood of this just man. Look you to it.

25.t: And the whole people answering, said:
His blood be upon us and upon our children.

26.t: Then he released to them Barabbas: and having scourged Jesus, delivered him unto them to be crucified.

27.t: Then the soldiers of the governor, taking Jesus into the hall, gathered together unto him the whole band.

28.t: And stripping him, they put a scarlet cloak about him.

29.t: And platting a crown of thorns, they put it upon his head, and a reed in his right hand. And bowing the knee before him, they mocked him, saying:

30.t: And spitting upon him, they took the reed and struck his head.

31.t: And after they had mocked him, they took off the cloak from him and put on him his own garments and led him away to crucify him.

32.t: And going out, they found a man of Cyrene, named Simon: him they forced to take up his cross.

33.t: And they came to the place that is called Golgotha, which is the place of Calvary.

34.t: And they gave him wine to drink mingled with gall. And when he had tasted, he would not drink.

35.t: And after they had crucified him, they divided his garments, casting lots; that it might be fulfilled which was spoken by the prophet, saying: They divided my garments among them; and upon my vesture they cast lots.

36.t: And they sat and watched him.

37.t: And they put over his head his cause written: THIS IS JESUS THE KING OF THE JEWS.

38.t: Then were crucified with him two thieves: one on the right hand and one on the left.

39.t: And they that passed by blasphemed him, wagging their heads,

40.t: Vah, thou that destroyest the temple of God and in three days dost rebuild it: save thy own self. If thou be the Son of God, come down from the cross.

41.t: In like manner also the chief priests, with the scribes and ancients, mocking said:

42.t: He saved others: himself he cannot save. If he be the king of Israel, let him now come down from the cross: and we will believe him.

43.t: He trusted in God: let him now deliver him if he will have him. For he said: I am the Son of God.

44.t: And the selfsame thing the thieves also that were crucified with him reproached him with.

45.t: Now from the sixth hour, there was darkness over the whole earth, until the ninth hour.

46.t: And about the ninth hour, Jesus cried with a loud voice, saying:
That is, My God, My God, why hast thou forsaken me?
46.q: the translation of the cry is the narrator's gloss per convention, as in Mark 15:34; could be voiced by Jesus

47.t: And some that stood there and heard said:

48.t: And immediately one of them running took a sponge and filled it with vinegar and put it on a reed and gave him to drink.

49.t: Let be. Let us see whether Elias will come to deliver him.

50.t: And Jesus again crying with a loud voice, yielded up the ghost.

51.t: And behold the veil of the temple was rent in two from the top even to the bottom: and the earth quaked and the rocks were rent.

52.t: And the graves were opened: and many bodies of the saints that had slept arose,

53.t: And coming out of the tombs after his resurrection, came into the holy city and appeared to many.

54.t: Now the centurion and they that were with him watching Jesus, having seen the earthquake and the things that were done, were sore afraid, saying:
Indeed this was the Son of God.
54.q: said by the centurion and those with him; given to the centurion alone so he keeps his voice from Mark and Luke

55.t: And there were there many women afar off, who had followed Jesus from Galilee, ministering unto him:

56.t: Among whom was Mary Magdalen and Mary the mother of James and Joseph and the mother of the sons of Zebedee.

57.t: And when it was evening, there came a certain rich man of Arimathea, named Joseph, who also himself was a disciple of Jesus.

58.t: He went to Pilate and asked the body of Jesus. Then Pilate commanded that the body should be delivered.

59.t: And Joseph taking the body wrapped it up in a clean linen cloth:

60.t: And laid it in his own new monument, which he had hewed out in a rock. And he rolled a great stone to the door of the monument and went his way.

61.t: And there was there Mary Magdalen and the other Mary, sitting over against the sepulchre.

62.t: And the next day, which followed the day of preparation, the chief priests and the Pharisees came together to Pilate,

63.t: Sir, we have remembered, that that seducer said, while he was yet alive: After three days I will rise again.
63.q: the chief priests and the Pharisees together; kept on the chief-priests voice

64.t: Command therefore the sepulchre to be guarded until the third day: lest perhaps his disciples come and steal him away and say to the people: He is risen from the dead. And the last error shall be worse than the first.

65.t: You have a guard. Go, guard it as you know.

66.t: And they departing, made the sepulchre sure, sealing the stone and setting guards.
